Abraham, emigrating with Sarah, calls her his sister before a tyrant king; her prayers leave the king seized whenever he approaches, and he sends her back with a slave-girl.
Abraham migrated with Sarah, who was given Hajar as a slave-girl, and Sarah said Allah had humiliated the pagan.
Abraham's plea for his father Azar on Resurrection Day is refused, Paradise being forbidden to disbelievers; the Prophet condemns Ka'ba pictures showing Abraham and Ishmael divining with arrows.
Abraham, tall in the Prophet's dream and resembling him, circumcised himself at eighty and lied only thrice, once shielding Sarah from a tyrant; a salamander blew the fire on him.
The Prophet said we have more right to doubt than Abraham, who asked Allah to show him how He gives life to the dead so his faith would be stronger.
On the Day of Resurrection Abraham sees his father's darkened face and reminds Allah of His promise not to disgrace him, and Allah says He has forbidden Paradise to disbelievers.
When a tyrant demanded Sarah from Abraham and sought to harm her, she made ablution and prayed, and the king was seized by a fit.
